hypotheses.text: Responsibility for rewards (whether rewards occurred following choices made by the participant or the partner) influences variations in happiness.
hypotheses.anchor: Crucial for our research question, we aimed to assess whether responsibility for these rewards, i.e., taking into account whether the rewards occurred following choices made by the participant or the partner, would also influence variations in happiness.

hypotheses.text: Participant happiness will decrease more following low lottery outcomes for the partner when the participant rather than the partner chose the lottery (interpersonal guilt).
hypotheses.anchor: To specifically search for a sign of interpersonal guilt, we analysed happiness values reported after outcomes of lottery choices in the Social and Partner conditions

hypotheses.text: Connectivity with regions showing guilt- and responsibility-related responses during outcomes will change depending on whether participants made decisions for themselves only or for themselves and their partner, and depending on the type of choice (Safe or Risky).
hypotheses.anchor: We hypothesized that connectivity with regions that showed guilt- and responsibility-related responses during the outcome phase (see previous paragraph) might change depending on whether participants made decisions for themselves only or for themselves and their partner, and depending on the type of choice (Safe or Risky).

hypotheses.text: Anterior insula activation will reflect interpersonal guilt (increased activation when participants are responsible for low outcomes for their partner).
hypotheses.anchor: To search for regions involved in this situation, we again analysed voxel responses using linear mixed models

hypotheses.text: Brain regions will be more engaged during decisions in the Social condition (affecting both self and partner) compared to the Solo condition (affecting only self).
hypotheses.anchor: we aimed to identify the brain regions associated with social decision-making under risk, and searched for regions more engaged during decisions in the Social condition compared to the Solo condition

hypotheses.text: Brain regions will respond more to partner reward prediction errors resulting from participant rather than partner choices.
hypotheses.anchor: We thus used this model to search for voxels responding more to partner reward prediction errors resulting from participant rather than partner choices
